real_estate.homebuilder: Mortgage rates eased Tuesday, but the 10-Year Treasury hit its highest level since 2002 this morning, and the local ledger now counts price change homes.
real_estate.commentary:
Mortgage rates got a one day breather. Mortgage News Daily's 30-year fixed eased to 7.56% Tuesday from Monday's 7.61%, and the 15-year to 7.22%. The 10-Year Treasury closed at 5.27%, down from 5.31%.

The breather looks short. This morning the 10-Year touched 5.35%, its highest level since April 2002 according to CNBC, so expect lenders to give back some of Tuesday's improvement today.

Locally, the five city ledger reads 685, up from 671, but that is mostly bookkeeping. Starting today it counts the 21 homes in price change status, which are still for sale and were being left out. On Tuesday's rules the count would be 664, seven fewer. The board wide table eased to 2,643 from 2,661.

What this means for you: at 7.56%, the five city median list price of $1,079,000 with 20% down runs about $6,071 a month in principal and interest, $392 more than on Sept. 1, when the 30-year was 6.89%. Buyers have leverage with the 150 homes that have sat 60 days or longer; ask for seller credits toward a rate buydown. Sellers who are not getting showings should price for today's payment, not for summer's.

• Board wide: 2,643 listings across our 15 city table, counting active and in contract together, with 167 coming soon and 170 brand new.

📍 Alameda County (Fremont Focus)

• Live ledger: 685 listings across Fremont, Hayward, Milpitas, Newark and Union City. 609 are on the market and 76 are coming soon. From today the ledger includes homes in price change status (21 today).
• Fremont: 244 live, 200 active, 29 coming soon and 15 brand new. The median on market list price is $1,275,000 at $797 a square foot, and the typical active listing has been out 30 days.
• The rest of the ledger: Hayward 183, Milpitas 108, Newark 88, Union City 62.
• Across all five cities the median is $1,079,000 at $680 a square foot. 286 homes are priced under a million, and 150 have been sitting 60 days or longer.

stocks.note: Levels are Tuesday, October 6 at the closing bell. Wednesday at 7:58 AM PT: S&P 500 -0.62%, Dow -1.03%, Nasdaq -0.79%.
stocks.news:
The S&P 500 closed above 7,800 for the first time Tuesday, a record at 7,818.93, and the Nasdaq set a second straight record close. It did not last the night: as of 7:58 AM PT Wednesday the Dow is down 1.03%, the S&P 500 down 0.62% and the Nasdaq down 0.79%, with Treasury yields at a 24 year high and the minutes of the Fed's September meeting due this afternoon.

The firms that run these markets are having a year to match. New York's Comptroller says NYSE member firms earned $45.9 billion before taxes in the first half of 2026, their best six months on record, and could top $90 billion for the year if the pace holds. Last year's record was $65.1 billion. Record bonuses are the expected next headline.

Abroad, Taiwan just took the year's top spot from South Korea. Taiwan's Taiex rose 3.9% last quarter while Korea's Kospi fell 19.3%, a 23 point swing, leaving Taiwan up 65.5% for 2026 through September and Korea up 62.3%. In May, Taiwan passed India to become the world's fifth biggest stock market at $4.95 trillion, by Bloomberg's count, carried by TSMC, the chipmaker behind much of Silicon Valley's AI hardware.

feature_images.alt: Bar chart of annual pretax profits of NYSE member firms: 2020 $50.9 billion, 2021 $58.4 billion, 2022 $25.8 billion, 2023 $26.3 billion, 2024 $49.9 billion, 2025 a record $65.1 billion. The 2026 bar shows $45.9 billion earned in the first half and a hatched projection to $90 billion or more if the pace holds. A dashed line marks the previous record, $61.4 billion in 2009.
feature_images.caption: Wall Street earned $45.9 billion in the first half of 2026, its best six months on record. If the pace holds, the year tops $90 billion, against 2025's record $65.1 billion.
feature_images.source: Source: Office of the New York State Comptroller, The Securities Industry in New York City (October 2026) and the October 2024 report. Pretax profits of NYSE member firms' broker and dealer operations.

feature_images.alt: Dot chart of benchmark index changes in 2026, at June 30 and at Sept. 30: Taiwan Taiex +59.3% to +65.5%; South Korea Kospi +101.1% to +62.3%; Japan Nikkei 225 +39.2% to +32.6%; U.S. S&P 500 +9.6% to +11.8%; Hong Kong Hang Seng minus 10.7% to minus 4.0%; China CSI 300 +7.5% to minus 5.9%; India Nifty 50 minus 8.7% to minus 13.4%. Last quarter Taiwan rose 3.9% and Korea fell 19.3%.
feature_images.caption: Korea led the world at midyear, up 101%. A 19.3% third quarter drop handed the lead to Taiwan, now up 65.5% for 2026 through September.

economy.note: All four are Tuesday, October 6: the Treasury daily yield curve close, the COMEX December gold and silver settlements, and the ICE December Brent settlement. Wednesday at 7:58 AM PT: 10-Year 5.30%, gold $4,130.40, silver $60.06, Brent $101.90. Market Briefs printed the 10-Year at 5.31% and rising, gold at $4,168 and falling, and Brent at $101.49; the official closes are on the cards.
economy.commentary:
The trade gap is back above $100 billion. The deficit in goods and services widened 13.7% in August to $105.6 billion, the widest since March 2025, when importers rushed goods in ahead of tariffs. Imports rose $17.2 billion, led by industrial supplies such as crude oil and gold, and capital goods such as semiconductors. For the year to date, the deficit is still 19.9% smaller than in 2025.

Taiwan, home of the chips, posted the third largest goods deficit with the U.S. in August, $18.3 billion, behind Mexico and Vietnam. Gold, meanwhile, slid this morning to its lowest level since early August, which CNBC tied in part to a stronger dollar.

feature_image.alt: Line chart of the monthly U.S. trade deficit in goods and services, January 2025 to August 2026. It peaks at $133.0 billion in March 2025 as imports rushed in ahead of tariffs, falls to about $60 billion by April, hits a low of $37.4 billion in October 2025, holds near $53 billion from January to April 2026, then climbs to $92.8 billion in July and $105.6 billion in August 2026, the widest since March 2025.
feature_image.caption: The deficit widened 13.7% in August to $105.6 billion, the widest since the March 2025 rush to beat tariffs. For the year to date it is still 19.9% smaller than 2025.
feature_image.source: Source: U.S. Census Bureau and Bureau of Economic Analysis, U.S. International Trade in Goods and Services, August 2026 (released Oct. 6, 2026), seasonally adjusted.

crypto.commentary: Bitcoin is down 4.21% over 24 hours near $82,900, Ether down 5.86% and XRP down 6.28%, live from CoinGecko at 7:58 AM PT.
